decisions.reason: The visual style and composition change does not alter the homepage's required sections or information goal.
Clean styling, large images, and generous spacing do not change the independently recorded mobile-friendly requirement.
The candidate already records the same-message color palette, national positioning, and cross-location consistency; the source layout change does not require another brand-identity update.
Visual layout and image-spacing choices do not change package or pricing consistency across locations.
The candidate already has a same-message update covering reusable, consistently designed location pages; the source's detailed visual style remains owned by the visual-layout requirement.
The source's visual-layout change does not affect domain routing, and the domain stated in the same message is already represented by a separate candidate event.
The location selector, selectable locations, and routing behavior are already represented by a same-message event and are not changed by the visual-style update.
Requesting large images and generous spacing does not determine which legacy images or content must be reused.
The visual-layout update does not change the SEO preservation goal or migration handling.
Visual presentation does not alter the requirement to keep the legacy site available or linked during transition.
The source's visual direction does not change where bookings occur or the separation of location booking systems.
A shared clean visual style is compatible with separate location websites and does not modify their architectural separation.
